reference_sql:
WITH april_orders AS (
  -- one row per order placed in April 2025 (UTC days of order_ts)
  SELECT order_id
  FROM orders
  WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01 00:00:00'
    AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-01 00:00:00'
), april_lines AS (
  -- one row per order line of those orders
  SELECT l.order_line_id, l.order_id, l.product_id
  FROM order_lines l
  JOIN april_orders a ON a.order_id = l.order_id
)
SELECT 'order_id is unique' AS check_name, COUNT(*) AS checked_rows, COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS failing_rows
FROM april_orders
UNION ALL
SELECT 'every order has a line', COUNT(*), COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_id NOT IN (SELECT order_id FROM april_lines))
FROM april_orders
UNION ALL
SELECT 'every line has a known product', COUNT(*), COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE product_id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM products))
FROM april_lines

WITH april_orders AS (
  -- one row per order placed in April 2025 (UTC days of order_ts)
  SELECT order_id
  FROM orders
  WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01 00:00:00'
    AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-01 00:00:00'
), april_lines AS (
  -- one row per order line of those orders
  SELECT l.order_line_id, l.order_id, l.product_id
  FROM order_lines l
  JOIN april_orders a ON a.order_id = l.order_id
)
SELECT 'order_id is unique' AS check_name, COUNT(*) AS checked_rows, COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS failing_rows
FROM april_orders
UNION ALL
SELECT 'every order has a line', COUNT(*), SUM(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM april_lines l WHERE l.order_id = a.order_id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
FROM april_orders a
UNION ALL
SELECT 'every line has a known product', COUNT(*), SUM(CASE WHEN l.product_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM products p WHERE p.product_id = l.product_id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
FROM april_lines l

solver.query:
WITH o AS (
  SELECT order_id FROM orders
  WHERE order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-04-01' AND order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-05-01'
)
SELECT 'order_id is unique' AS check_name,
  COUNT(*) AS checked_rows,
  COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS failing_rows
FROM o
UNION ALL
SELECT 'every order has a line',
  COUNT(*),
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_lines l WHERE l.order_id = o.order_id))
FROM o
UNION ALL
SELECT 'every line has a known product',
  COUNT(*),
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE l.product_id IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM products p WHERE p.product_id = l.product_id))
FROM o JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id
